revision: 2026-09-01b: split into a fixed-shape PRIMARY gating case and a free-nu SECONDARY structural-finding case, after Totoro run suite-run-01/a6-run (logs a6-1/2/3.log) surfaced an honest structural mismatch on the original single free-nu comparison.
gap_it_closes: docs/dev-log/core070/parity-panel-2026-09-01.md finding 4: the shared A6 harness cell sat both engines on the nu->infinity boundary; R correctly diagnosed it (false-convergence(8)), Julia missed it (converged=true at nu=3.0e31). This contract's fixture is deliberately genuinely heavy-tailed so BOTH engines are expected interior, isolating the health-wiring repair from the boundary pathology itself (which remains a separate, honestly-reported finding wherever it recurs).

totoro_finding_2026-09-01b.observed: gen and R stages both exit 0; the paired compare failed HONESTLY -- not a numeric near-miss but a structural mismatch: R's student() with df=NULL estimates a degrees-of-freedom PARAMETER PER TRAIT (length p=5 vector), while GLLVM.jl's default disp_group=:shared fits ONE shared degrees-of-freedom across all traits. Loadings differed at ~0.05, model-mismatch scale (two different models fit to the same data, not the same model fit twice), matching the class of the NB2 benchmark's shared-r-vs-per-trait-phi lesson.
totoro_finding_2026-09-01b.r_readback_verification: R/gllvmTMB.R:167-168 documents this explicitly: 'The student() family fits one log-sigma and one log(df-1) per trait (df > 1; pass student(df = 3) to fix df at 3'. Confirmed as genuine documented behaviour (not a quirk) by reading the per-trait pin machinery directly, R/fit-multi.R:5317-5349 (dispersion_trait_family_mask + dispersion_trait_map for both log_sigma_student and log_df_student, with an explicit per-trait df_pin loop when the user supplies a numeric df). CRITICAL SECOND FINDING while verifying: sigma_student is ALSO always per-trait in R, unconditionally -- passing a numeric df pins ONLY log_df_student per trait (R/fit-multi.R:5325-5342, 'If the user supplied numeric df ... pin log_df_student per trait'); it does NOT collapse sigma_student to one shared value. This means the naive fix (just add nu=6.0 on the Julia side, leaving disp_group=:shared) would STILL have mismatched sigma shape (Julia 1 value vs R 5 values) even after pinning nu. The corrected fixed case therefore also switches the Julia side to disp_group=:species (per-trait sigma, matching R unconditionally) while pinning nu=6.0 as a scalar (matching R's df=6 pin, which sets every trait's df to the identical scalar value).

julia_health_wiring.before: StudentTFit.nu_boundary was additive only (commit efe3d644): converged semantics unchanged, so a boundary fit could still present as converged=true.
julia_health_wiring.after: fit_studentt_gllvm forces converged = converged && !nu_boundary (mirrors _tweedie_verdict's :power_at_boundary rule, families/tweedie.jl), which flows into the GENERIC family-agnostic fit-health gate (sanity_multi / gllvmTMB_diagnose, diagnostics.jl) via fit.converged with no diagnostics.jl edit needed. Tightens the gate only; no existing pass case is affected.
julia_health_wiring.unit_test: GLLVM._studentt_nu_boundary and the conv && !boundary composition, test/test_studentt_boundary.jl
julia_health_wiring.red_first_fixture_test: pure-Gaussian data (test/test_studentt_boundary.jl, 'red-first: near-Gaussian data walks estimated nu to the boundary'; same construction as test_studentt_boundary_honesty.jl) -- asserts fit.converged == false, sanity_multi(fit).pass == false, gllvmTMB_diagnose(fit).pass == false when the boundary is reached

fixture_design.family_r: student(link = "identity")  (R/families.R:367-381; estimates degrees of freedom unless df is supplied)
fixture_design.family_julia: StudentTFamily()  (src/families/studentt.jl; identity link, nu estimated by default)
fixture_design.generator: tools/core070_a6_studentt_fixture.jl generate_fixture(rng): y_tj = beta_t + Lambda_t * z_j + sigma_true * eps_tj, z_j ~ N(0,1) iid across sites, eps_tj ~ standard t(nu_true) (Distributions.TDist). The SAME generated response matrix feeds both the fixed and free cases below.
fixture_design.design_note: nu_true = 6 is deliberately, genuinely heavy-tailed (not the pure-Gaussian construction used to exercise the boundary in test_studentt_boundary.jl / test_studentt_boundary_honesty.jl) -- both engines are expected to converge to an INTERIOR nu on this fixture. A local plumbing check (no real R; a synthetic 'R' file built from Julia's own fitted coordinates) reproduced converged=true, nu_boundary=false for both cases, with the fixed case's nu pinned exactly at 6.0 and the free case recovering nu_hat approx 5.89, sigma_hat approx 0.699 -- close to nu_true=6.0, sigma_true=0.7 -- confirming the fixture is well-conditioned and estimable at this size before any live R run.

fixed.role: PRIMARY, GATING -- determines the script's exit code
fixed.r_call: student(link = "identity", df = 6)  -- pins log_df_student at log(5) for EVERY trait (R/fit-multi.R:5325-5342)
fixed.julia_call: fit_studentt_gllvm(Y; K = 1, nu = 6.0, disp_group = :species)  -- FAMILY-09-FIXED-SHAPE path (the nu::Real branch of fit_studentt_gllvm), with disp_group = :species so sigma is per-trait (matching R's unconditional per-trait sigma_student)
fixed.matched_model: Both sides: per-trait sigma (length p), ONE scalar nu = 6.0 shared identically across every trait (R re-reports that identical scalar once per trait via df_student; Julia keeps it as a single Float64 -- the comparator broadcasts the Julia scalar against every R per-trait entry, see 'nu_comparison_note' below). No structural mismatch remains.
quantities_compared: df_student (per-species df, length p, all values expected == 6.0)
loading (per-species Lambda, sign-aligned for the K=1 indeterminacy)

both_engine_health_required.r: healthy == 1 (inline health check: optimizer convergence code 0, finite objective/parameters/gradient, scaled gradient <= 1e-3, sigma_student finite and > 0, df_student not at the nu_boundary_max = 1e6 Gaussian-limit boundary) AND nu_at_boundary == 0
both_engine_health_required.if_either_fails_on_this_interior_fixture: recorded as a finding in a6-studentt-notes.md / the Totoro run's own output, never silently fudged, tolerance-widened, or dropped from the comparison (round2-3 #11's explicit instruction)

fixed.nu_comparison_note: Julia's fixed-nu fit reports fit.ν as a single Float64 (nu is not per-trait when passed as a Real, independent of disp_group); R's report$df_student is always length p. tools/core070_a6_studentt_fixture.jl's _a6_compare broadcasts the Julia scalar against every entry of R's per-trait vector rather than requiring equal lengths -- a reporting-shape difference, not a real model mismatch, since nu was pinned identically on both sides.

free.role: SECONDARY, NON-GATING -- printed for the record, never affects the exit code
free.r_call: student(link = "identity")  -- df = NULL, R's documented per-trait-estimated default
free.julia_call: fit_studentt_gllvm(Y; K = 1)  -- disp_group = :shared (default): ONE shared sigma and ONE shared nu across all traits
free.classification: dispersion_structure_finding (see below) -- NOT a pass/fail numeric gate. Two different models (per-trait vs shared dispersion structure) are fit to the same data on purpose, to keep this divergence visible and documented rather than silently dropped from the harness.
reported_not_asserted: loglik (both sides, plus an informational delta)
nu (Julia's single shared value vs R's p per-trait values)
sigma (Julia's single shared value vs R's p per-trait values)

dispersion_structure_finding.class: Same class as the NB2 benchmark's shared-r-vs-per-trait-phi lesson: GLLVM.jl's disp_group kwarg (:shared default vs :species) must be set to match whichever dispersion structure the frozen R family actually fits by default, or the comparison is between two different statistical models, not two implementations of the same one.
dispersion_structure_finding.r_default_confirmed_documented_evidence: R/gllvmTMB.R:167-168 (docstring, unconditional: 'The student() family fits one log-sigma and one log(df-1) per trait') + R/fit-multi.R:5317-5349 (the actual per-trait map/pin machinery for both log_sigma_student and log_df_student) -- read directly from the local gllvmTMB checkout, not inferred from behaviour alone.
dispersion_structure_finding.julia_default_is_shared: fit_studentt_gllvm(...; disp_group = :shared) is GLLVM.jl's own default (src/families/studentt.jl), chosen independently of R's default at the time StudentTFamily was implemented.
dispersion_structure_finding.julia_matching_path_exists: disp_group = :species gives GLLVM.jl per-trait sigma AND (when nu is also estimated, i.e. nu = nothing) per-trait nu -- structurally matching R's free-nu default. This leaf does NOT switch the 'free' case to disp_group = :species: round2-3 #11 asked to keep the free-nu case as a recorded structural finding at its ORIGINAL (default-vs-default) configuration, not to fix it into a second gating case. A disp_group = :species free-nu paired case is a natural follow-up leaf, not built here.
dispersion_structure_finding.recommendation_for_future_leaves: Any new paired R/Julia family fixture should state its dispersion-structure alignment (shared vs per-trait, for every family that has a disp_group choice) explicitly in its contract BEFORE running the comparison, not discover it from a failed harness cell.

argv_convention.r_stage: Rscript --vanilla tools/core070_a6_studentt_fixture.R <data_path> <r_output_path>  (argv 2; K and the fixed-case pinned nu are fixed in-script, not runtime arguments; fits BOTH cases -- fixed then free -- in one invocation, writing case-prefixed keys fixed_... / free_... to one output file)
argv_convention.julia_stage: julia --project=. tools/core070_a6_studentt_fixture.jl <data_path> <r_output_path>  (argv 2; run once to generate <data_path> if missing, again after the R stage to verify; fits BOTH cases in one invocation) OR julia --project=. tools/core070_a6_studentt_fixture.jl --self-test (synthetic pair for the fixed/gating case only, no data/R required)

coverage_guard: the Julia stage refuses to report a pass while r_output_path is missing (exit 1, CORE070_A6_STUDENTT_AWAITING_R) -- a missing oracle side is never silently treated as agreement. Applies to the whole invocation (both cases are read from the same file).
soft_fail: read_r_output raises on any line it cannot parse as a scalar or indexed-vector key/value row rather than skipping it silently; read_r_result raises (Julia KeyError, not a silent skip) if a required case-prefixed key is absent from the R output; _a6_compare treats any missing required key on either side as a hard failure before any numeric comparison runs, for the fixed/gating case.

self_test.scope: exercises _a6_compare only (the fixed/gating case's comparator); the free case has no tolerance gate to self-test, by design
self_test.revision_note: the synthetic pair was updated to the realistic 'fixed' case shapes (Julia sigma length p, Julia nu length 1 broadcast against R's length-p df_student) after the disp_group=:species correction; one new mutation exercises the nu-broadcast comparison path directly (a single R per-trait df_student entry moved past tolerance).
